intro: Art is where I find my voice. I paint the quiet moments we often miss, from the light on an ancient temple wall to the unguarded look on a face, in watercolour, graphite, ink and pastel.

bio: Hey, I’m Abrar Abir. I grew up in a coastal village in Bagerhat, Bangladesh, where the rhythms of nature and tradition shaped my worldview. While I am often defined by my work in science research and leadership, art is where I truly find my voice. Deeply influenced by Sanatani traditions and the rich history of South Asian artistry, I strive to capture the fleeting moments we often miss—the way light hits an ancient temple wall or the quiet, unguarded look on a person’s face.

My work is a dialogue between the past and the future. I explore my heritage through paintings of divine figures and architecture, yet I also drift into the imaginary, designing futuristic characters that blur the line between human and machine. Whether I am studying the weight of a pose in a sketch or the shadows on a simple piece of fruit, my goal is always the same: to tell an honest story, be it a calm river scene or a gritty vision of the future.

artworks.title: The Potter’s Hands
artworks.description: This painting is about the focus and rhythm of craftsmanship. I chose to use vibrant, warm tones on the potter to show the life and energy he puts into his work. It’s a tribute to the humble beauty of creating something by hand—a skill passed down through generations that still feels vital and alive today.

artworks.title: The Devotee
artworks.description: A study of the intimate bond between the mortal and the divine. By juxtaposing the vivid, iconic presence of Goddess Durga with the quiet, earthly posture of the seated woman, the work explores how faith provides a sanctuary of inner peace amidst cultural vibrancy.

artworks.title: Life on the Water
artworks.description: A bird’s-eye perspective of traditional river boats, capturing the organized chaos of river life. The composition emphasizes the geometric beauty of the vessels, symbolizing the flow of commerce, community, and the persistent current of daily survival.

artworks.title: Steps of Ancients
artworks.description: This piece captures the vertical majesty of temple architecture rising from the ghats. It serves as a tribute to historical endurance, where every brick and spire tells a story of centuries of pilgrimage and the unwavering spirit of the city.

artworks.title: Sci-Fi Characters
artworks.medium: Fine-liner ink and pen on paper
artworks.description: A collection of speculative character designs blending organic human forms with complex mechanical exoskeletons and tactical gear. These sketches explore a future where technology is scavenged and integrated into daily survival, highlighted by intricate line work and high-contrast shading.

artworks.title: Whispers of Buddha
artworks.description: A spiritual portrait of the Buddha radiating an ethereal, warm aura. The soft transitions of color symbolize the expansion of consciousness and the transition from the material shadows into the light of ultimate wisdom.

artworks.title: The Tandava of Lord Shiva
artworks.description: An exploration of divine kinesis, capturing the rhythmic “Tandava” dance of Lord Shiva. The piece utilizes high-energy cross-hatching to represent the vibrating energy of the universe, where creation and destruction exist in a singular, powerful moment of balance.

artworks.title: The Quiet Table
artworks.description: This piece is a study of the simple things that make up a home—a bottle, some fruit, and a glass of wine. I was interested in how light plays across different surfaces, like the shine on an apple versus the soft folds of a cloth. It’s meant to feel like a calm, stolen moment in the middle of a busy day, reminding us to slow down and notice the colors in the objects we use every day.

artworks.title: The Studio Sanctuary
artworks.description: A “painting within a painting” that captures a solitary artist at work in a sun-drenched courtyard. It explores the concept of the artist as an observer, documenting the harmony between man-made architecture and the sprawling, untamed beauty of nature.

artworks.title: Human Figures
artworks.description: A series of academic figure studies focusing on the seated male form. These sketches utilize triangular compositional framing and structural line-work to explore the physical weight, muscle tension, and quiet dignity of the human body in repose.

artworks.title: The Pensive Sari
artworks.description: A portrait focusing on the “Bhava” or mood of the subject. The cool blue tones of the saree contrast with the earthy textures of the background, highlighting a moment of deep, personal introspection tucked away in a natural setting.

artworks.title: Indigo Morning
artworks.description: Fishermen setting out through the river fog before the day has fully begun. Working in a single indigo, I let the water carry the pigment and dissolve the far bank into mist, so the boats feel half-remembered, the way mornings by the river felt in the village where I grew up.

artworks.title: Shade and Blossom
artworks.description: A woman rests against the trunk of an old tree, flowers woven into her hair and a single white blossom held loosely in her hand. Painted in the soft, muted palette of traditional South Asian miniatures, the piece is about stillness: the private, unhurried moment when the day pauses and the mind is allowed to wander.

artworks.title: Lines of a Lifetime
artworks.description: A charcoal portrait of an elderly man set against layered leaves and fallen blossoms. Every crease and shadow on his face was built up slowly, line over line, to read like a record of the years he has lived: weathered, unguarded, and quietly dignified.

artworks.title: The Waiting Boat
artworks.description: A lone wooden boat rests in the shallows beside a sunlit sandbank, its mooring poles standing in the green water. It is a scene from the riverside life I grew up with: loose, fresh brushwork for the trees, and quiet reflections that make the whole river feel as if it is holding its breath.

artworks.title: Beneath the Trees
artworks.description: Two figures walk together along a tree-lined path, small against the canopy above them. Built entirely from directional hatching, the drawing turns sunlight and shadow into rhythm, and leaves the people at its centre a moment of companionship that needs no words.
